summary: MISO and its Transmission Owners ask FERC to hold the E-8 show cause proceeding in abeyance for 90 days, through November 16, 2026, while they use the Large Load Working Group to prepare a series of section 205 filings.
ask: Hold the proceeding in abeyance for 90 days starting August 17, 2026, with a shortened answer period and expedited treatment.

points.point: The movants say the stakeholder process needs the 90 days to craft section 205 filings answering the order.
points.quote: The Motion is necessary to permit MISO and the MISO Transmission Owners to continue the MISO stakeholder process to develop and submit FPA section

points.point: MISO says some issues in the order were not in its original workplan, and the 60-day deadline blocks stakeholder development.
points.quote: The current, imminent compliance deadline in the Show Cause Order effectively prohibits the full development and robust consideration of any potential stakeholder solutions to integrating large loads.

points.point: Planned filings: a Zero Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement, a large load definition, interconnection reliability requirements, a firm step-up service and a parallel load and resource study (LARS).
points.quote: a parallel study process for large load and generation resources (i.e., Load Addition and Resource Study process or “LARS”)

points.point: MISO expects to file the ZGIA by the end of August.
points.quote: MISO expects to submit the ZGIA filing by the end of August.

points.point: LARS would study load and generation in parallel within 120 days and address the order's proximate generation concern.
points.quote: The studies will be run in parallel, and will finish at approximately the same time—within 120 days

points.point: MISO expects to file the firm service step-up Tariff revisions by November 16, 2026, or earlier if feasible.
points.quote: MISO expects to make a section 205 filing proposing Tariff revisions incorporating the firm service step-up option by November 16, 2026, or earlier, if feasible.

points.point: The Large Load Working Group has six scheduled meetings before the abeyance ends.
points.quote: the LLWG is scheduled to meet six times between the date of this filing and the end of the requested abeyance period

throughLine.text: Uses the abeyance option in the E-8 order (P 37) to postpone the 60-day show cause deadline and lays out the filings MISO plans, including LARS for proximate generation and a firm step-up service.

figures.label: Requested abeyance period
figures.quote: hold this proceeding in abeyance for a period of 90 days starting August 17, 2026
